title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page continues a setup of the transcendental (complex-analytic) moduli of elliptic curves.

**Setting.** S is a complex analytic space and E/S a relative elliptic curve. H = R^1 or H_1, the local system of first (co)homology, is a rank-2 local system of Z-modules. H⊗R carries the complex structure coming from Lie(E), i.e. from H⊗R ≅ Lie(E) as real bundles.

**Torelli structure.** A 'structure de Torelli' is a trivialization t: Z_S^2 ≅ H, i.e. a global frame (z_1, z_2). In modern terms this is a Teichmüller or full-homology marking, a 'level ∞' structure. The previous page noted that framed objects are rigid. This page completes the sentence: the set of isomorphism classes of framed relative elliptic curves over S is in canonical bijection with the set of holomorphic maps τ: S → C∖R (5), where τ = z_2/z_1 in the complex line H⊗R.

**Strict structures.** The structure is called 'directe' or 'stricte' if at every point the frame (z_1, z_2) is positively oriented for the orientation induced by the complex structure. Equivalently, τ lands in the upper half-plane D+ = {Im z > 0} (6). Hence D+ is the fine moduli space, in the analytic category, of elliptic curves with oriented framing.

**Universal family.** The universal family is X_{D+} = (D+ × C)/Z^2, where Z^2 acts by T_{m,n}(τ, z) = (τ, z + m + nτ) (7)-(8). Its fiber over τ is C/(Z + Zτ). Via z ↦ exp(2πiz) this fiber is ≅ C*/k^Z with k = exp(2πiτ) and |k| < 1, i.e. the Jacobi/Tate multiplicative uniformization.

**Next page.** SL(2,Z) acts on the right on framings, t ↦ t∘g. The next page computes the induced action τ' = (dτ + b)/(cτ + a), with an unusual matrix convention.

**Purpose.** This is the classical preparation for describing the analytic moduli stack of elliptic curves as [SL(2,Z)\D+], or a quotient by a congruence subgroup. It belongs to notes on moduli of elliptic curves in characteristic ≠ 2, presumably intended to compare the algebraic Legendre/level-2 picture with the transcendental one.
errors: Equation number (8) is used twice on the page; minor numbering slip.

Implicit identification: z_1, z_2 are sections of H (a local system), and τ = z_2/z_1 makes sense via the complex structure on H⊗R (equivalently Lie(E)). The bijection with holomorphic maps S → C∖R needs holomorphy of the complex structure in families. This is standard but not argued.
Next-page formula τ' = (dτ+b)/(cτ+a) is correct for the stated convention z'_1 = a z_1 + c z_2, z'_2 = b z_1 + d z_2, though the convention is non-standard (a transposed/permuted Möbius action).

ideas.what: Framings of H_1 (Torelli/Teichmüller structure) make relative elliptic curves rigid, with fine analytic moduli space C∖R; with orientation condition, the upper half-plane
ideas.modern_name: Teichmüller space of genus 1 / upper half-plane as fine moduli of marked elliptic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Riemann, Klein, Teichmüller); in families: Grothendieck's Cartan seminar 1960-61 exposés on Teichmüller theory
ideas.where_published: Séminaire Henri Cartan 13 (1960/61), 'Techniques de construction en géométrie analytique' (Teichmüller spaces)

ideas.what: Universal family (D+ × C)/Z^2 with T_{m,n}(τ,z) = (τ, z+m+nτ)
ideas.modern_name: Universal framed elliptic curve over the upper half-plane

ideas.what: Fiber C/(Z+Zτ) ≅ C*/q^Z with q = e^{2πiτ}, |q|<1

deep.surprise_reason: Entirely classical textbook material: the upper half-plane as fine moduli of oriented-framed elliptic curves, the universal family and the q-uniformization. It is written out carefully, but nothing here is new or uncredited.
